## The George Wendt Show (1995)
Almost every actor from the [_Cheers_ cast](https://www.cinemablend.com/television/the-cheers-characters-ranked-by-who-id-personally-most-like-to-drink-with) would go on to find further success with their own hit sitcom but George Wendt is a surprising exception. The beloved multi-Emmy nominee's self-titled comedy, adapted from a popular radio show called _Car Talk_, was canceled after CBS aired only six of the eight episodes that were produced.
![Image 13: Eddie Griffin and Malcolm-Jamal Warner standing in front of a bar on Malcolm &amp; Eddie](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MfYua3rDychKkSTw3cfyHi.jpg)
(Image credit: TriStar Television)
texts.12:
## Malcolm & Eddie (1996-2000)
In the early days of UPN, one of the network's most successful sitcoms was _Malcolm & Eddie_, which followed the mismatched titular duo as roommates and business partners. However, these days, Malcolm-Jamal Warner is still best known as _The Cosby Show_'s Theo and at least Eddie Griffin has his stand-up and movies like _Undercover Brother_ on his resume.
![Image 14: Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen standing next to each other on Two of a Kind](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/rWh3dj9BYFEX98UXXpKTEi.jpg)
(Image credit: ABC)
texts.13:
## Two Of A Kind (1998-1999)
After becoming household names by playing the same character, Michelle Tanner, on _[Full House](https://www.cinemablend.com/tag/full-house)_ for eight seasons, the Olsen Twins would later share the screen in their own ABC sitcom, _Two of a Kind_. The show cast the siblings in their own roles this time – twin sisters also named Mary-Kate and Ashley – but their star power could not keep it running for more than one season.
![Image 15: John Caponera looking up at Drew Carey with a towel around his neck on The Good Life](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/iAULaU4jMkdi4domMhQQHi.jpg)
(Image credit: NBC)
texts.14:
## The Good Life (1994)
Before Drew Carey hit it big with his ABC sitcom, he starred in a supporting role in the short-lived NBC comedy, _The Good Life_. Lasting one 13-episode season, the show followed the personal and professional life of a lock distribution warehouse middle manager played by John Caponera.
![Image 16: Carey Lowell on A League Of Their Own](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/nga7G77qtJoyb7uykfMbRH.jpg)
(Image credit: Columbia Pictures Television)

## A League of Their Own (1993)
A widely [forgotten TV show based on a movie](https://www.cinemablend.com/television/forgotten-tv-shows-based-on-movies) is CBS' _A League of Their Own_, which actually brought back a few cast members from the classic sports movies, but not [Tom Hanks](https://www.cinemablend.com/tag/tom-hanks) or Geena Davis, which may have cost it a life beyond five episodes. The story of the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League's development in World War II would later inspire an acclaimed, but also short-lived, Amazon Prime original series in 2022.

## A Family For Joe (1990)
In early 1990, NBC aired a TV movie called _A Family for Joe_, which starred Robert Mitchum as a homeless man enlisted by a group of orphaned children to pose as their grandfather so they wouldn't be split up into foster homes. Soon after, the network adapted the story into a sitcom, which only lasted nine episodes, but notably starred future Oscar nominee Juliette Lewis and Ben Savage before he led the [_Boy Meets World_ cast](https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2567022/what-the-boy-meets-world-cast-is-up-to-now).
![Image 18: Faizon Love and Robert Townsend on The Parent 'Hood](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/qsAgfhHUobwngqUHLBYjd6.jpg)
(Image credit: The WB)

## The Parent 'Hood (1995-1999)
_The Parent 'Hood_ starred co-creator Robert Townsend as a former English professor left to run the house as his wife (Suzzanne Douglas) returns to the workforce. Also starring comedian Faizon Love, the show's _Mr. Mom_-esque premise kept audiences interested for four seasons but, despite becoming available with a [Max subscription](https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2570432/subscribing-to-hbo-max-what-to-know-about-the-price-options-and-what-the-streaming-service-offers) for some time, it has since become one of The WB's more obscure comedies.

(Image credit: ABC)

## Good & Evil (1991)
In the 1970s, ABC aired a sitcom that cleverly poked fun at daytime soap opera conventions called _Soap_, which proved to be a groundbreaking hit. When the network tried the concept again with _Good & Evil_, starring Teri Garr as a vain heiress and Margaret Whitton as her selfless sister, it only lasted 11 episodes.

(Image credit: CBS)

## High Society (1995-1996)
With multiple Emmy wins to her name, Jean Smart is concerned a television icon but not everything on the _Hacks_ star's resume has been a bonafide hit. Take, for example, _High Society_, which boasts a similar premise to U.K.'s _Absolutely Fabulous_ (starring Smart and Mary McDonnell as two outrageous socialites) but was not quite as successful, lasting one 13-episode season on CBS.
![Image 21: Thomas Gibson and Jenna Elfman standing together with looks of concern in Dharma and Greg.](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/nL2wvWSaU2DUNbVYYJGnfR.jpg)
(Image credit: 20th Century Fox Television)

## Dharma & Greg (1997-2002)
_Dharma & Greg_ starred Jenna Elfman and Thomas Gibson as the titular couple, who could not be more different but find love with each other anyway. The fun and romantic sitcom ran for five seasons on ABC but, when compared to to co-creator by [Chuck Lorre](https://www.cinemablend.com/tag/chuck-lorre)'s later projects (i.e. _Two and a Half Men_ and _The Big Bang Theory_) it has a considerably more obscure legacy.
![Image 22: Tom Arnold in a gym on The Jackie Thomas Show](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/uYf7zhzf7LRCUjzfppHBth.jpg)
(Image credit: ABC)

## The Jackie Thomas Show (1992-1993)
After acquiring fame through his marriage to sitcom star [Roseanne Barr](https://www.cinemablend.com/tag/roseanne-barr), Tom Arnold teamed up with his then-wife to create and executive produce his own vehicle called _The Jackie Thomas Show_. For just 18 episodes, Arnold led the ABC original show business satire as an unlikable sitcom star.
![Image 23: Joey Lawrence standing in a doorway on Brotherly Love](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/yVHK2HUYUKozxw7mBkPQSh.jpg)
(Image credit: Touchstone)

## Brotherly Love (1995-1997)
Joey Lawrence stole the show on _Blossom_, but his follow-up, _Brotherly Love_, was not quite as successful and only lasted two seasons – one on NBC and the second on The WB. However, we imagine he still had fun starring on the sitcom with his younger brothers, Matthew and Andy, who play the half-siblings he reunites with following the death of their father.

(Image credit: Warner Bros. Television)

## Life With Roger (1996-1997)
_Life with Roger_ starred Mike O'Malley in the title role – a homeless man convinced not to take his own life by a doctor named Jason (Maurice Godin), who eventually becomes his roommate. It lasted only one season on The WB, but O'Malley would become better known anyway for a more successful CBS sitcom called _Yes, Dear_ and for his role in the [_Glee_ cast](https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2560631/what-the-glee-cast-is-doing-now) as Kurt's dad, Burt Hummel.
![Image 25: Lori Loughlin and Tony Danza in a police station on Hudson Street](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TP6HNRr62SZZyTFdBbXZ2i.jpg)
(Image credit: ABC)

## Hudson Street (1995-1996)
Already practically sitcom royalty from the respected success of _Who's the Boss?_ and _Full House_, Tony Danza and Lori Loughlin teamed up to lead _Hudson Street._ Following the romance between a divorced homicide detective (Danza) and a crime reporter (Loughlin), the otherwise well-received sitcom suffered from dwindling ratings and, after ABC moved it to a Saturday timeslot, its first season also became its last.
![Image 26: Valerie Harper on the phone on The Office](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4rADsBvJiMyh5vfxhHcqBi.jpg)
(Image credit: CBS)

## The Office (1995)
While not to be confused with NBC's _The Office_ or its U.K. predecessor, this short-lived CBS sitcom was, coincidentally, an Americanized update of a British sitcom called _Upstairs, Downstairs_. Lasting just six episodes, it followed a group of executives and assistants working at a packaging company played by a recognizable cast of actors including _The Mary Tyler Moore Show_'s Valerie Harper, [Batman voice actor](https://www.cinemablend.com/superheroes/batman/the-10-best-batman-voice-actors-ranked) Kevin Conroy, and future [_That '70s Show_ cast](https://www.cinemablend.com/television/what-the-that-70s-show-cast-is-doing-now) member Debra Jo Rupp.
![Image 27: Shelley Long and Robert Hays on Kelly Kelly](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/dAVszdudYKgSbWHz4BooHi.jpg)
(Image credit: Warner Bros. Television)

## Kelly Kelly (1998)
Shelley Long never quite achieved the same level of notoriety that she acquired when playing Diane Chambers to Emmy-winning acclaim on _Cheers_ after leaving in 1987. One of the most obscure examples is _Kelly Kelly_, where she plays a literature professor whose first name also becomes her last when she marries a widowed fire chief played by Robert Hays.
![Image 28: Al Franken on LateLine](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/QPTj3WDkZLpYjsUZq2fCg5.jpg)
(Image credit: NBC)

## LateLine (1998-1999)
Best known for his tenure as an _SNL_ writer and cast member and his later political career, Al Franken once had an NBC sitcom, too, called _LateLine_. Taking place behind the scenes of a late-night news program in the vein of _Nightline,_ it ran for two seasons on NBC, with unaired episodes later appearing on Showtime.
![Image 29: Rob Schneider on Men Behaving Badly](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/NJvimyeKUzzYMovuqqMePU.jpg)
(Image credit: NBC)

## Men Behaving Badly (1996-1997)
The first [sitcom starring _SNL_ cast member](https://www.cinemablend.com/television/sitcoms-starring-snl-cast-members-after-they-left-the-show) Rob Schneider after leaving Studio 8H was _Men Behaving Badly_. He and Ron Eldard played college friends indulging in childlike behavior alongside Justine Bateman the girlfriend of one of them, who is forced to put up with their antics.
![Image 30: The cast of Love and Marriage](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/5UDzrPZJGCSDpdhgKZpmKE.jpg)
(Image credit: Fox)
texts.29:
## Love And Marriage (1996)
Along her way to achieving wide acclaim with _Gilmore Girls_ and _The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel_, Amy Sherman-Palladino hit a bump in the road. The first series she ever created, _Love and Marriage_ – which starred Tony Denison and Patricia Healy as a couple raising a family in New York – lasted only three episodes on Fox.
![Image 31: James Garner wearing a suit in Man Of The People](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ZjkRWnoyBotzek87k3JYth.jpg)
(Image credit: NBC)
texts.30:
## Man Of The People (1991-1992)
Years after his success with shows like _Maverick_ and _The Rockford Files_ and before he landed a supporting on _8 Simple Rules_, James Garner led a comedy called _Man of the People_. Lasting 10 episodes on NBC, the series followed a womanizing grifter appointed to the city council, where he comes at odds with the mayor, played by Kate Mulgrew.
![Image 32: Jake Steinfeld looking accomplished with the Big Brother Jake cast](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/9imHMLN3Zp7gCJxSGoFyHi.jpg)
(Image credit: North Star Entertainment Group)
texts.31:
## Big Brother Jake (1990-1994)
The first original sitcom from The Family Channel, which would come to be known as Freeform many years later, was _Big Brother Jake_. It starred Jake Steinfeld as a former Hollywood stuntman who returns to his Brooklyn foster home to help out his recently widowed foster mother.
![Image 33: Ed Asner with his TV family on Thunder Alley](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/mrDA4fpBWTHvF23BWGgFJi.jpg)
(Image credit: ABC)

## Thunder Alley (1994-1995)
Playing Lou Grant on _The Mary Tyler Moore Show_ (and on the more dramatic but equally good spin-off, _Lou Grant_) made Ed Asner a celebrated television icon. However, one of his most rarely acknowledged credits is _Thunder Alley_, an ABC sitcom in which he starred as a retired racecar driver.
